learning_objective: 🎯 Add color and excitement to your sentences with adjectives and learn how to compare different things!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Adjectives are describing words that give us extra, colorful details about a noun. Instead of just saying 'I saw a dog', an adjective lets you say 'I saw a huge, fluffy, brown dog!'
This is the simple, basic form of an adjective. We use the Positive degree when we are just describing one single person, animal, or thing, like 'The tree is tall'.
When we want to compare exactly two things, we use the Comparative degree. We usually add '-er' to the word, like 'The oak tree is taller than the apple tree'.
When we compare three or more things, we use the Superlative degree to show which one is the most extreme! We usually add '-est', like 'The redwood is the tallest tree in the whole forest'.

fun_activity.title: 🥇 The Ultimate Comparison
fun_activity.instructions: Pick three of your family members or friends. Write sentences comparing their heights using the words tall (Positive), taller (Comparative), and tallest (Superlative)!

quick_recap: ⭐ Adjectives add exciting details and descriptions to nouns and pronouns.
⭐ We use Positive for one thing, Comparative for two things, and Superlative when comparing three or more things!
